what: The YouTube Thumbnail Downloader shows every size of a video's thumbnail image from a link or video ID: maximum resolution (1280 × 720), standard (640 × 480), high (480 × 360), medium (320 × 180) and small (120 × 90).

It understands every common link form, including watch?v=, youtu.be, Shorts, embed, live and music links, links with extra parts such as &t= or &list=, and the plain 11-character ID. Sizes a video does not have are detected and hidden automatically.

The images load straight from YouTube's public image server into your browser. Thumbnails are the creator's work, so respect copyright: use them for reference, commentary or with permission. This tool is not affiliated with YouTube or Google.
uses: Study how successful channels design thumbnails before you make your own.
Get back a full-size copy of a thumbnail you uploaded and lost.
Use a thumbnail with credit when writing about or reviewing a video, where fair use or permission applies.
Show a video's cover image in slides with a link to the video.
See whether a video has a sharp HD thumbnail or only lower sizes.
tutorial: In YouTube, copy the address from the browser bar, or tap Share then Copy link in the app. Shorts and live links work too.
Paste into "YouTube video link or ID". The thumbnails load automatically, or click "Get thumbnails".
The line under the box shows the 11-character video ID it found and how many sizes are available.
The largest available size appears first. Sizes the video does not have, often the maximum resolution on older videos, are hidden.
Click "Open full size" to view it in a new tab, or "Download" to save it as a .jpg file named after the video ID and size.
Some browsers block downloads from another site. The tool then shows an "Open the image" link: open it, then right-click (or long-press on a phone) and choose "Save image".
features: watch, youtu.be, Shorts, embed, live, music, mobile and attribution links, with or without extra parameters.
From 1280 × 720 down to 120 × 90, with real dimensions shown.
YouTube returns a grey placeholder for sizes that do not exist; the tool spots it and hides that size.
Saves the image with a clear filename like VIDEOID-maxresdefault.jpg.
Clear instructions when a browser blocks direct downloads.
Nothing to install; the images come straight from YouTube's image server.

example.title: Worked example: saving your own old thumbnail
example.text: You uploaded a video in 2015 and lost the original thumbnail file. You copy the link https://youtu.be/abcdefghijk?si=share and paste it. The tool shows "Video ID: abcdefghijk. 4 sizes available (this video has no maximum resolution version)". The largest is Standard 640 × 480, so you click Download and get abcdefghijk-sddefault.jpg.

tips: Use the maximum resolution version when it exists. It is the only true HD 16:9 size.
Standard and high quality sizes are 4:3 and may have black bars at the top and bottom.
Only use other people's thumbnails with permission, for commentary or within fair use, and credit the channel.
If a video was just uploaded or its thumbnail just changed, the new image can take a while to appear.
A private or deleted video usually has no thumbnails.
problems: "Could not find a YouTube video ID"
The text is not a YouTube link. Copy the full link from the address bar or the Share button, or paste just the 11-character ID.
The video may be private, deleted or the ID mistyped. If you are offline, the images cannot load.
The maximum resolution size is missing
Older or low-resolution videos often have no 1280 × 720 thumbnail. Use the next largest size.
Download opens a message instead of saving
Your browser blocked the direct download. Click "Open the image", then right-click or long-press and choose "Save image".
